text:
Brandt Clarke has 14 points in 21 games, and our numbers think he's been shortchanged. The Kings have scored 8.0 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, and a gap like that usually swings back.

The work underneath is excellent. At five-on-five Los Angeles takes 56.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, and is far better with him than without. That matches last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him 1.7 wins above replacement, 36th among 215 defensemen, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 99th percentile of defensemen for primary shot assists.

He's 23 and playing almost 20 minutes a night, six of his points on the power play, and our projection puts his season somewhere around 46 points. The last ten games read six assists and no goals, which fits a defenseman who sets up more than he shoots. If his teammates start finishing the chances he helps create, those assists are the first place it should show.
headline: Brandt Clarke is setting up goals that aren't going in
